content: One such database is the National Reporting and Learning System (NRLS), a central repository of patient safety incident reports from the NHS in England and Wales. Set up in 2003, the NRLS now contains more than 13 million detailed records. The incidents are reported using a set of standardised categories and contain a wealth of organisational and spatio-temporal information (structured data), as well as, crucially, a substantial component of free text (unstructured data) where incidents are described in the `voice' of the person reporting. The incidents are wide ranging: from patient accidents to lost forms or referrals; from delays in admission and discharge to serious untoward incidents, such as retained foreign objects after operations. The review and analysis of such data provides critical insight into the complex functioning of different processes and procedures in healthcare towards service improvement for safer carer.
